---
title: Geometry
---

### Setting
A user can specify one or multiple **geometry files** in the [settings.toml](../../settings/index.qmd). It is advisable to give descriptive names to the geometry files, e.g., *buildings.fgb* or *roads.fgb*. Most-used file types are GeoPackages or Shapefiles but more file types are accepted as can be seen at the bottom of this page.

::: {.callout-tip title="Example"}
Make sure that each geometry file gets it's own entry in the settings.toml file.
:::

When providing a polygon or line geometry file, a user can choose to use the *area extraction method* for considering water levels or depths over the whole area of the asset. This can be more appropriate than point estimates for example for large buildings.

::: {.callout-warning}
Assets cannot be partially or fully outside the hazard map extent! FIAT will stop if it detects any.
:::

Each geometry file is linked to exactly **one** vulnerability dataset via the `vulnerability` entry of its `[[exposure]]` entry (a single name, by default `default`). The dataset may hold 1D or 2D curves; its [method](../vulnerability.qmd#methods) determines the needed hazard types and columns. Methods that combine several datasets (e.g. `flood.depth_duration`) can not be used for geometries.

```toml
[[exposure]]
file = "exposure/spatial.fgb"
area_method = "area"
vulnerability = "default"
```

#### Output
The output geometry file holds, per hazard identifier `<id>` (the band number for an event, the return period for risk), a column per hazard value of the method (e.g. `depth_<id>`, and `duration_<id>` for the depth-duration method), a column per impact column (e.g. `damage_structure_<id>`) and the total per impact type (e.g. `total_damage_<id>`). In case of a risk calculation the expected annual damage is added per impact type: a column `ead` when there is a single impact type, `ead_<type>` (e.g. `ead_damage`) per impact type otherwise.

#### Supported data formats
An overview of supported formats is presented [here](../supported.qmd#geometry-files)

### Tabular information
In the table down below, an overview is provided od the necessary inputs in either the vector file.

| Field                                                  | Required | Multiple | Example                   |
|--------------------------------------------------------|----------|----------|---------------------------|
| [object_type](#object_type)                            | No       | -        | residential               |
| [fn_< any >_< any >](#vulnerability-curves)            | Yes      | Yes      | struct_2                  |
| [elevation](#elevation)                                | Yes      | -        | 0.5                       |
| [reference](#reference)                                | No       | -        | 4                         |
| [max_< any >_< any >](#maximum-value)                  | Yes      | Yes      | 193457.00                 |
: exposure input {#tbl-exposure .hover}

A more detailed description of the data fields can be found below.

#### Object Type
The type of the object according to the type of the vector dataset, e.g. occupancy type for a building dataset.

#### Vulnerability curves
The user can input as many vulnerability curves and related maximum values as required. However, at least one vulnerability curve and related maximum value must be provides per asset. Vulnerability curve column are named as `fn_< exposure_type >_< component >` (for exposure types, see [here](../../settings/optional.qmd#exposure-geom)). This name can be chosen freely but it is recommended to give it a descriptive name, such as **damage** (exposure type) in combination with **structure** or **content** (components), and it is required to use the same name in the maximum value column. (i.e. `max_< exposure-type >_< component >`) The value that must be entered is the name of the vulnerability curve, relating to the curve ids of the vulnerability dataset linked to the geometry file in the [vulnerability file](../vulnerability.qmd). Globally, continental vulnerability curves can be obtained from [European Commission's Joint Research Centre](https://publications.jrc.ec.europa.eu/repository/handle/JRC105688), but it is recommended to use more location-specific functions when available.

#### Elevation
The elevation of the object (e.g. the ground floor height) relative to the surface. It is subtracted from the water depth at the object. Required by all flood [methods](../vulnerability.qmd#methods).

#### Reference
The reference (height) of the surface compared to the hazard data, e.g. the ground elevation. It is used to convert a water level to a water depth.

::: {.callout-important}
 Only required for the method `flood.level`, see the [methods](../vulnerability.qmd#methods).
:::

#### Maximum value
The maximum value corresponds to the vulnerability curves for each asset. For each vulnerability curve type that was assigned, a maximum value must also be assigned. These values represent the maximum damage to, for example, the structure, content, or other (e.g. inventory). There are methods to derive these values, based on building type and area of the building. Globally, maximum damage values per country can be obtained from [European Commission's Joint Research Centre](https://publications.jrc.ec.europa.eu/repository/handle/JRC105688), but it is recommended to use more location-specific damage values. In the US, [FEMA Hazus](https://www.fema.gov/flood-maps/products-tools/hazusis) is an industry standard in how to derive these values.
